newsitem.title: INDIA: State Bank of India employees end strike.
newsitem.headline: State Bank of India employees end strike.

text.p: Agitating staff of the State Bank of India on Thursday called off a six-day-old strike after the bank's management agreed to review orders to suspend three officers, a spokesman for the employees' union said.

"We have withdrawn the agitation after management have agreed to review the suspension of three officers in connection with the CRB Capital Markets cases within two months," B.B. Das, a senior member of the State Bank of India Officers' Federation, told Reuters.
Das said the union and the management of India's largest public sector commercial bank signed an agreement at 2:30 a.m. on Thursday (2200 GMT Wednesday) to end the strike.
The decision was announced hours before the bank's board of directors met in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta to finalise its results for the year ending March 31, 1997.
Talks to end the strike failed on Tuesday, and the union said the stir, which began in Bombay on June 12, would cover 13 regional headquarters on Thursday.

The union was protesting against the suspension of three officers accused of failing to follow proper procedures in handling the accounts of CRB Capital Markets, a finance company now facing liquidation proceedings. The management had also agreed to review all other cases of suspension, Das said.
